get.summary: Health check endpoint.
get.description:
Probes the server's external dependencies (currently just the database)
rather than reporting a static liveness value: a healthy result is `200`,
while any failing dependency yields `503 Service Unavailable` with a
`"degraded"` status so orchestrator health checks and monitors react to a
dependency outage.

Note what is gone relative to the Salvo implementation: there is no
"server state unavailable" arm. `Inject<AppState>` cannot fail, so the
third branch the old handler needed -- a depot miss it reported as
degraded -- is not a state this can reach.

get.summary: Poster, backdrop or thumbnail art for one title.
get.description:
Beam fetches the image from the metadata provider once and serves it from
its own cache thereafter, so a viewer's browser never contacts TMDB or
AniList and those CDNs never see who is looking at what (ADR-0015).

The URL is stable across re-enrichment; the strong `ETag` is what changes
when a title's artwork does, so clients revalidate rather than re-download.
A title with no art, an id that does not exist, and a variant that does not
apply to this kind of title are all `404` -- every client already renders a
placeholder for that. An id that is not a UUID is a `400`, as on every
other route that takes a media id.

Asks the IdP for a device code, keeps it, and hands the client an opaque
handle plus the user code to display. The user approves on any other
device; the client polls `POST /v1/auth/device/token` meanwhile.

post.description:
Each call reaches the IdP at most once, and not at all when it comes
sooner than the flow's interval allows -- that answers `slow_down` and
grows the interval, as RFC 8628 section 3.5 has the IdP do. On approval
the session is minted exactly as the browser callback mints it (same
admin claim, JIT provisioning, disabled gate, and expiry) and its opaque
value returned in the body, to be presented as the `beam_session` cookie
on every later request.

get.summary: Prometheus text exposition of everything the installed recorder collected.
get.description:
Unauthenticated, and deliberately so: it is only as reachable as
`BEAM_BIND_ADDRESS`, and the supported deployment keeps that internal behind
a reverse proxy which does not forward `/metrics` (see
`docs/operations/deployment.md`).

Described rather than hidden. Salvo let this be a plain `Handler` that
`merge_router` could not see, so it stayed out of the spec by accident of
the framework. Kynos routes and describes from one declaration, and the only
ways to keep it out would be the `unchecked` feature -- which stamps the
*whole* document non-authoritative to hide one route -- or a second listener
on its own port. Describing it under an `internal` tag is the honest option,
and satisfies the readiness contract's requirement that internal routes be
explicitly marked.

List of unique streams associated with this movie. Empty in a browse
result, which does not read files; the detail route fills it.

file_id.description:
Identifier of the primary streamable file, if any. Absent in a browse
result, as `streams` is empty there.

stream_url.description: Direct-play stream URL for this file (Range-request capable, inline).

download_url.description: Download URL for this file (Range-request capable, `Content-Disposition: attachment`).

MediaSource.description:
One playable/downloadable version of a media item. Beam models multiple
deliverable qualities/editions as distinct source files rather than
transcoding on demand (see ADR-0004: never live-transcode); this is how a
client picks among them for constrained-bandwidth playback.

MediaSortField.description: Sort field options for media search.

has_next_page.description: Whether a page follows this one.

has_previous_page.description: Whether a page precedes this one.

start_cursor.description: Cursor of the first item; absent on an empty page.

end_cursor.description: Cursor of the last item; absent on an empty page.

PageInfo.description: Where a page sits in the whole listing.

page_info.description: Where this page sits in the whole listing.

MediaConnection.description:
One page of browse or search results.

`items` are in the requested order. `page_info`'s cursors are opaque: pass
`end_cursor` as `after` for the next page, `start_cursor` as `before` for
the previous one, with the same `sort_by` and `sort_order`.

ContinueWatchingItem.description:
One row in the continue-watching list. `media_id`/`media_type` let the
client link to the detail page; `episode_id` is set only for episodes, so
the client can additionally deep-link to the right episode within a show.

HistoryItem.description:
One row in the watch-history list. Same resolved shape as
[`ContinueWatchingItem`] but additionally carries `completed`, since history
lists finished items too (continue-watching filters them out).

HistoryResponse.description:
A page of watch history. `total` counts the user's history rows (completed
and in-progress) whose file is present, so the client can paginate; a row
whose file is missing from disk is in neither `items` nor `total`. `items`
may still hold fewer than the requested `limit` when a row's title can no
longer be resolved (that row is skipped here but still counted in
`total`).

PlaybackClientKind.description:
What kind of client reported: a browser family or a native platform,
never a version or user agent.

file_id.description:
The source (file) that started. Resolved to its container, codecs and
resolution class, then discarded.

audio_track_index.description:
Which of the source's `audio_tracks` (as `GET /v1/media/{id}/sources`
lists them, from 0) played. Absent, or out of range: the default track,
else the first.

file_id.description: The source (file) that failed. Resolved, then discarded.

audio_track_index.description: Which of the source's `audio_tracks` was chosen, as for a start.

PlaybackStartFailureEvent.description: A playback that failed to start.

file_id.description: The source (file) that was playing. Resolved, then discarded.

duration_ms.description: How long playback stalled, 1 ms to 10 minutes.

PlaybackRebufferEvent.description:
Playback stalled mid-stream waiting for data. A stall before the first
frame is part of starting, not a rebuffer.

PlaybackSwitchTrigger.description: What made the player switch source.

PlaybackSourceSwitchEvent.description: The player moved from one source of a title to another.

PlaybackTelemetryBatch.description:
What `POST /v1/telemetry/playback` takes: one client's events since its
last report, at most 50 in total. An omitted list is empty.

A client batches and flushes on its own schedule; the server counts each
event under the UTC day it arrives and forgets the file it named. An event
whose file the server cannot resolve -- unknown, or missing from disk -- is
dropped, not refused.

size.description: Number of media items in the library

last_scan_file_count.description: Number of files found in the last scan

FileContentType.description: The kind of content a media file represents

path.description:
Path of the file relative to its library's root, '/'-separated. Never
absolute (NFR-108).

hash.description:
Content hash (XXH3) as a decimal string. Identifies the file's content
for caching and duplicate detection.

content_type.description: What kind of content this file represents

scanned_at.description: When this file was first scanned

updated_at.description: When this file was last updated

LibraryFile.description: A media file within a library

total_count.description: Files the walk found to index; absent until the walk has finished.

processed_count.description: Files handled so far, whatever became of them.

added_count.description: Files indexed for the first time.

changed_count.description: Indexed files whose content changed, or which probed at last.

unchanged_count.description: Indexed files found as they were.

deferred_count.description: Files still being written, left for a later visit.

failed_count.description: Files that could not be processed.

marked_missing_count.description: Files no longer on disk, newly marked missing.

relinked_count.description:
Files found at a new path -- moved or renamed -- that kept their
row, and with it their id, progress and title.

purged_count.description: Files missing for the whole grace period, removed.

ScanProgress.description: A scan's per-file counts so far.

failure.description: Why a failed scan failed. Names no filesystem path.

ScanJob.description:
One scan of one library. A library has at most one queued or running
scan; the latest is kept until the server restarts.

details.description:
Structured context an operator can read, whose shape depends on the
event that produced it.

`Unchecked` because it genuinely is unconstrained: a scan failure and an
enrichment failure put different keys here. Kynos refuses a bare
`serde_json::Value` in a described type -- the schema would be `true`,
which is a claim the document cannot check -- and this wrapper says so
out loud instead, annotating the property `x-kynos-unchecked`. It is
`#[serde(transparent)]`, so the bytes on the wire are unchanged.

ScanPhase.description: Which moment of a scan an event reports.

ScanEvent.description: The scan job a `scan_progress` event reports on (FR-208).

scan.description:
The scan job a `scan_progress` event reports on; `null` on every
other category.

disabled.description:
Local moderation switch (see `PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id}`): a disabled
user cannot log in and their sessions are revoked on disable.

AdminUserDto.description:
One user row in the admin users tab. `is_admin` is informational and
read-only here: admin is derived from the IdP-asserted claim on every
login, so there is deliberately no endpoint to change it.

total.description: Total number of users across all pages.

UpdateAdminUserRequest.description:
Body of `PATCH /v1/admin/users/{id}`. `disabled` is the only mutable
field: `is_admin` is IdP-claim-driven (recomputed at every login), so a
local toggle would be silently overwritten and is deliberately absent.

EnrichmentQueueCounts.description: Metadata-enrichment queue overview: row counts per state.

RecentScanDto.description:
One recent library-scan admin log entry, slimmed to what the system
status tab renders.

LibraryWatchMode.description: How a library's changes reach the index between full rescans.

LibraryPollReason.description: Why a library is polled rather than natively watched.

watch_limit_reached.description:
Whether a native watch has hit the OS watch limit since the server
started. The libraries affected are polled; raising the limit
(`fs.inotify.max_user_watches` on Linux) and restarting watches them
natively again.

watch_limit_count.description:
The Linux per-user inotify watch limit (`fs.inotify.max_user_watches`),
`null` where it cannot be read.

libraries.description: Every library, in the order the library list returns them.

WatcherStatus.description: The filesystem watcher's state, for the admin system-status tab.

uptime_secs.description: Whole seconds since the server process built its state.

recent_scans.description: Most recent `library_scan` admin log entries, newest first.

watcher.description: How the filesystem watcher observes each library.

LibraryCountBucket.description:
The order of magnitude a count falls into. A report never carries an exact
count.

LibraryReportFiles.description: Present files by what the indexer classified them as.

name.description:
A container or codec name, lowercased, as FFmpeg names it; `unknown`
when the prober could not name it.

LibraryReportCount.description: How many of one named thing a library holds.

LibraryReportCodecs.description: Streams of present files, per codec.

LibraryFileSizeBucket.description: The size range one file falls into.

LibraryReportFileSize.description: How many present files fall into one size range.

LibraryTotalSizeBucket.description: The range the server's indexed bytes fall into. Never reported exactly.

schema_version.description: This report's shape; see the operator documentation.

server_version.description: The Beam release that produced the report.

generated_on.description:
The UTC day the report describes. A day rather than an instant, so the
moment of sending says nothing about when the server is running.

seasons.description: Seasons with at least one present episode file.

containers.description: Present files per container, sorted by name.

file_sizes.description: Present files per size range, smallest first; every range is listed.

LibraryReport.description:
The anonymous library report: what a server holds, in aggregate, every
number as a range.

destination_configured.description:
Whether `BEAM_TELEMETRY_URL` is set. When false nothing is ever sent;
the preview is still available, to decide whether to opt in.

destination_origin.description:
`scheme://host[:port]` of the collector; its path and query are not
shown, since they may carry an ingest token.

last_sent_at.description: When a report last reached the collector.

next_send_at.description: When the next report is due, once the schedule is running.

content_type.description: The `Content-Type` the payload is sent under.

payload.description:
The exact request body that would be sent: the report encoded as
OTLP/HTTP JSON metrics.

LibraryTelemetryPreview.description:
What `GET /v1/admin/telemetry/library` answers: the report this server
would send now, byte for byte, and whether and where it would go.

PlaybackTelemetryTotals.description: Totals across every row of the report.

PlaybackHeightClass.description:
The vertical resolution class of a file's video: `sd` under 720
lines, `hd` from 720, `fhd` from 1080, `uhd` from 2160.

container.description: Container, lowercased as FFmpeg names it; `unknown` when unnamed.

video_codec.description: Codec of the first video stream; `none` when there is none.

audio_codec.description: Codec of the audio stream that played; `none` when there is none.

PlaybackStartCount.description: Successful starts under one combination of dimensions.

PlaybackStartFailureCount.description: Failed starts under one combination of dimensions and one reason.

PlaybackBitrateClass.description: The average bitrate class of a whole file.

PlaybackRebufferBucket.description: The duration range one rebuffer fell into.

PlaybackRebufferBucketCount.description: How many rebuffers fell into one duration range.

histogram.description: Every duration range, shortest first, including empty ones.

PlaybackRebufferCount.description: Rebuffers under one combination of dimensions.

PlaybackSourceSwitchCount.description: Source switches under one combination of dimensions.

enabled.description:
Whether `BEAM_PLAYBACK_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` is on -- whether clients'
reports are being counted now. Counts kept while it was on remain
readable after it is turned off.

retention_days.description: How many days counts are kept after the day they count.

PlaybackTelemetryReport.description:
What `GET /v1/admin/telemetry/playback` answers: the daily counts from
`from` to `to` (UTC days, both inclusive), summed across the days.

Every list is sorted by its count, largest first, then by its dimensions.
No row names a user, a file or a title.

SessionSummary.description:
One of the current user's active sessions, as returned by `GET
/sessions`. `id` is an opaque row identifier for revocation via `DELETE
/sessions/{id}` -- never the session credential itself, which is hashed
at rest and cannot be recovered.

device_handle.description:
Opaque, single-flow secret the client polls `POST
/v1/auth/device/token` with. Only its SHA-256 is stored.

user_code.description: The code the user enters at `verification_uri`.

verification_uri.description: Where the user approves the sign-in, on any device with a browser.

verification_uri_complete.description:
`verification_uri` with the code filled in, when the IdP offers one --
suitable for a QR code.

expires_in_secs.description: How long the user has to approve, in seconds.

interval_secs.description: The minimum wait between polls, in seconds.

DeviceLoginStart.description:
What `POST /v1/auth/device` answers: what to show the user, and the handle
to poll with.

The IdP's device code is not here. Beam keeps it and polls the IdP itself,
so a client can only ever turn an approval into a Beam session -- never
into IdP tokens (ADR-0003's BFF property, kept for native clients).

session_token.description:
The `beam_session` credential. Present it as the `beam_session`
cookie on every later request; it is the same opaque session a
browser login mints, with the same idle and absolute expiry.

session_expires_in_secs.description: The session's hard lifetime from now, in seconds.

DeviceLoginComplete.description: A device login the user approved: the session it minted.

DeviceLoginWait.description: Why a device login is still waiting.

interval_secs.description: The minimum wait before the next poll, in seconds.

DeviceLoginPending.description: A device login that has not finished yet.

BeamSession.name: beam_session
BeamSession.description: Opaque session cookie issued by the OIDC login flow (ADR-0003). Hashed at rest; never recoverable from the API.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, sessions, and the current user

tags.description: Operational endpoints outside the client contract
